falsification_tests: A grade entered in this study's records that is not one of P1-P4 as spec.md section 2 states them; a grade entered without its decisive evidence cited in the evaluation record; a record of this study presenting the hypothesis as assumed, as dismissed by posture, or as proven impossible.
claims.text: The hypothesis statement of spec.md section 1, the four predictions of section 2, the grading rule of section 3, and the two evidence legs of section 4 are the evaluation of this study, and no grade in this study was entered under any other design. Does not establish: that the four predictions exhaust what the hypothesis could predict under a different formulation, or that the grading scale is the only defensible one; the claim registers this evaluation's design and its discipline, not the hypothesis's fate under every formulation.

falsification_tests: A demonstrated shared derived feature set (sign forms with values, structural conventions, or numerical practices) among two or more of the three systems, traceable to a common ancestor and exceeding what chance and independent invention predict; or a re-run of the filed measurement under its filed feature set showing the trio clustering against the controls.
claims.text: P1 (cross-system inheritance) is NOT SUPPORTED: the documented derivations give the three systems three separate, local, mutually unrelated origins (Meroitic from Egyptian hieroglyphic and demotic forms; the Cypriot syllabary from Cypro-Minoan in the Linear A tradition; the Indus script from local antecedent marks with no demonstrated external parent); their numerical practices share no convention beyond the tally principle; and the distributional measurement filed at records/p1-measurement-raw-output.json finds no clustering of the three systems' structural profiles relative to the program's deciphered control and a matched synthetic null (within-trio mean distance 3.819 vs trio-to-controls mean 3.643, on the filed feature set). Does not establish: that no contact ever occurred between the cultures (contact is documented and is not common descent), or that a paleographic comparison could not be run with data the program does not hold (C111-7).

falsification_tests: A demonstration that a named phase in one of these precursor sequences does not exist, is misdated out of sequence, or does not connect to the script it precedes (e.g. that the Ravi/Kot Diji marks bear no relation to the mature Indus signary, shown against the excavated corpus).
claims.text: P2 (developmental discontinuity) is NOT SUPPORTED: each script has local developmental precursors in the stratified or documentary record: Indus antecedent marks in the Ravi phase (c. 3300-2800 BCE) continuing through the Kot Diji phase (c. 2800-2600 BCE) into the mature script at Harappa; the Cypriot syllabary preceded by roughly five centuries of Cypro-Minoan on the same island; the Meroitic script preceded by centuries of Egyptian writing in Kush and derived from Egyptian forms. Does not establish: that development was smooth, continuous in every generation, or uninfluenced by contact; only that the precursor trails P2 requires to be absent are present.

falsification_tests: A written artifact, signs in sequence in a system ancestral to a program script, from a sealed, independently dated context materially before 3400 BCE, published with its dating and its ancestral relation demonstrated; or a peer-reviewed demonstration that one of the three labeled cases is a language-encoding script ancestral to a later tradition.
claims.text: P3 (chronological anomaly) is NOT SUPPORTED: no script in the program and no demonstrated direct ancestor of one is securely dated materially earlier than the standard chronology allows; the earliest Indus antecedent marks (c. 3300 BCE) are contemporary with proto-cuneiform and inside the standard account; and the claimed older writing cases (Jiahu marks, Vinca symbols, the Dispilio tablet) stand in the scholarly record as sign use or proto-writing not demonstrated to encode language, none of them ancestral to a program script. Does not establish: that no older sign use existed (it demonstrably did), or that an earlier find is impossible; only that none currently meets the prediction's terms.

falsification_tests: A demonstrated reading of an earliest-stratum text of any of the three traditions encoding astronomical, mathematical, or calendrical knowledge beyond that culture's independently documented attainment at that date.
claims.text: P4 (content residue) is NOT SUPPORTED overall: the earliest readable texts of the Eteocypriot and Meroitic traditions carry ordinary content within their cultures' documented attainment (the Amathus bilingual's civic-religious dedication; Meroitic royal and funerary formulae on Egyptian-derived templates); the Indus leg is UNTESTABLE in content while the script is unread, and unsupported in form, since the corpus's brevity (derivation-set mean 4.2 signs per text) cannot carry the treatise content P4 requires. Does not establish: anything about the content of the unread Indus corpus beyond its format limits, or about later texts of any tradition (P4 grades the earliest stratum).

claims.text: The distributional measurement is as filed: the measurement at records/p1-measurement-harness.py, run on the Spec 105 custody token streams and the Spec 107 Latin donor text under its declared six-feature set, returns the profiles and distances filed at records/p1-measurement-raw-output.json (SHA-256 6022f09a...): within-trio mean distance 3.819, trio-to-controls mean 3.643, Meroitic-Latin the closest program-system pair at 3.130; and its limits (small system count, one real control, the Eteocypriot derivation subset of 14 texts / 69 tokens, Latin sentence-texts) are stated on its face. Does not establish: that a richer feature set or a larger control set could not find structure this measurement misses; it is a descriptive, low-power leg, and the claim is about its fidelity, not its sufficiency.

claims.text: P1's paleographic leg is UNTESTABLE ON CURRENT EVIDENCE: the program holds no comparable sign-shape dataset (form features with provenance) for the three systems and their documented parents, so no shape-similarity measurement was run; the evaluation record section 5 states what acquiring the data would take, including that Indus sign images are statistics-only under the CISI terms this program observes. Does not establish: that the paleographic question is unanswerable in principle, or that the published derivations (which are substantially paleographic arguments) are weak; only that the program cannot currently run the leg itself.

falsification_tests: A material cost or explanatory gain of the hypothesis, on evidence available at the evaluation date, that the accounting omits.
claims.text: The closing accounting is as filed: the evaluation record section 7 states what the hypothesis explains that the standard account does not (near-simultaneous emergence and recurrent Neolithic sign use, both of which the standard account also addresses), what it costs in unsupported assumptions (a pre-3400 BCE literate civilization leaving no written artifact; a transmission channel crossing more than eight thousand years unattested; recipient traditions independently producing the local precursor trails the standard account predicts), and the single most decision-changing piece of new evidence (a sealed, independently dated pre-3400 BCE written artifact demonstrably ancestral to a program script). Does not establish: that the balance could not change with new evidence; the accounting is dated 2026-11-27 and is re-gradable on any find of the kind C111-4's falsifier names.
